problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 2 & -1 & 3 & -2 \\ -1 & 1 & 2 & -3\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{42}$ equal to zero.*
worked_solution:
Let's make entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{42}=1$ equal to zero using elementary column operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 2 & -1 & 3 & -2 \\ -1 & 1 & 2 & -3\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+{C}_{2} \\ {C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+(-2){C}_{2} \\ {C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+3{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & -3 & 7 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & -1 & 5 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $4$th row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & -3 & 7 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & -1 & 5 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{4+2}|\begin{aligned}5 & -3 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & 5 & -5\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}5 & -3 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & 5 & -5\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$
